title: Biotech breakthrough: Placenta makes 100-years old the new 60, research finds Business
text:
Biotech breakthrough: Placenta makes 100-years old the new 60, research finds By Julia Limitone Published February 15, 2018 Health Care FOXBusiness 
Facebook Twitter Print video Using living cells to treat diseases Celularity co-founders Peter Diamandis and Dr. Robert Hariri on the company's research into using living cells to treat cancer, autoimmune and degenerative diseases. 
Celularity, a leading U.S. biotechnology company, is seizing on an opportunity to use cells to target diseases.  The CEO, Dr. Robert Hariri, says placenta can be used to augment longevity and immunity.
Continue Reading Below
“The vision here is how do we have a healthier longer life and how do we use these stem cells and immunological cells to help fight cancers,” Celularity Vice Chairman Dr. Peter Diamandis said to FOX Business’ Maria Bartiromo on “Mornings with Maria.”
Hariri, previously the CEO of Celgene ( CELG ), which develops and commercializes medicines for cancer and inflammatory disorders, said mapping the genome was a key educator for where we are with diseases today.
“We have greater insights into the greater things which are the molecular basis for disease and we’ll be able to decipher and decode that before and be able to intervene before a disease occurs,” he told Bartiromo.

Research found placenta is the richest source of stem cells and can be used as a way to turn living cells into medicines aimed to treat cancer, autoimmune diseases, and degenerative disease and eventually regrow organs.
“At the heart of the aging process is a loss, and exhaustion, of the engine that drives the natural repair processes — it keeps us young,” Hariri said.
